title.value: A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b proof-of-concept clinical trial in early Alzheimer’s disease with lecanemab, an anti-Aβ protofibril antibody
title.quote: A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b proof-of-concept clinical trial in early Alzheimer’s disease with lecanemab, an anti-Aβ protofibril antibody

design.value: randomized double-blind clinical trial, utilized a Bayesian design with response-adaptive randomization
design.quote: randomized double-blind clinical trial, utilized a Bayesian design with response-adaptive randomization

n.quote: A total of 854 randomized subjects were treated

population.value: early Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild AD dementia
population.quote: early Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild AD dementia

biomarker_confirmation.value: amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ 1–42
biomarker_confirmation.quote: All subjects were confirmed amyloid positive via amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ 1–42 for eligibility.

followup.quote: Study 201 ( NCT01767311 ) was an 18-month, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled Bayesian design clinical trial

intervention.value: lecanemab (2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, 10 mg/kg biweekly)
intervention.quote: five lecanemab arms (2.5 mg/kg biweekly, 5 mg/kg monthly, 5 mg/kg biweekly, 10 mg/kg monthly, 10 mg/kg biweekly)

n_description.quote: A total of 854 randomized subjects were treated

outcomes.name: 12-month clinical change on the Alzheimer’s Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS) for the ED90 dose
outcomes.quote: At 12 months, the 10-mg/kg biweekly ED90 dose showed a 64% probability to be better than placebo by 25% on ADCOMS, which missed the 80% threshold for the primary outcome.
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The primary endpoint was Bayesian analysis of 12-month clinical change on the Alzheimer’s Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS)

outcomes.name: change from baseline at 18 months in brain amyloid by PET Standard Uptake Value ratio (SUVr)
outcomes.quote: The respective LS mean differences from placebo for the individual lecanemab treatment groups were −0.099, −0.136, −0.201, −0.229, and −0.310 ( P < 0.001 for all doses).
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Key secondary endpoints were change from baseline at 18 months in brain amyloid by PET Standard Uptake Value ratio (SUVr)

outcomes.name: change from baseline on ADCOMS over 18 months
outcomes.quote: In the conventional analyses, lecanemab showed dose-dependent reduction in change from baseline on ADCOMS over 18 months (Figure S), with 30% ( P =0.034) less clinical decline compared to placebo at 10 mg/kg biweekly
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Key secondary endpoints included... clinical decline on ADCOMS

outcomes.name: Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum-of-Boxes (CDR-SB)
outcomes.quote: Lecanemab reduced clinical decline on CDR-SB, with 26% less decline ( P =0.125) at 10 mg/kg biweekly and 17% ( P =0.255) with 10 mg/kg monthly, compared to placebo, but these differences did not reach nominal significance
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Key secondary endpoints included... Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum-of-Boxes (CDR-SB)

outcomes.name: Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog14)
outcomes.quote: Lecanemab at 10 mg/kg biweekly reduced clinical decline on ADAS-Cog14 (Fig. c) over 18 months, with 47% ( P =0.017) less decline compared to placebo.
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Key secondary endpoints included... Alzheimer’s Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog14)

primary_endpoint_status.quote: BAN2401-G000-201 did not meet the 12-month primary endpoint.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The 10-mg/kg biweekly dose showed a 64% probability of being 25% better than placebo on ADCOMS at 12 months, missing the required 80% probability threshold.

harms.name: symptomatic ARIA-E
harms.quote: There were 5 cases of symptomatic ARIA-E (lecanemab: 5/46 [11%])

harms.name: ARIA-H
harms.quote: ARIA-H (new cerebral microhemorrhages, cerebral macrohemorrhages, and superficial siderosis) regardless of the presence of ARIA-E were observed in 13 (5.3%) subjects in the placebo group ( N = 245)

harms.name: ARIA-H
harms.quote: compared to 65 (10.7%) subjects in the lecanemab groups ( N = 609)

harms.name: ARIA-H
harms.quote: the incidence of ARIA-H on lecanemab was higher in ApoE4 carriers ( N = 436) (57 [13.1%] subjects)

harms.name: ARIA-H
harms.quote: than in ApoE4 non-carriers ( N = 173) (8 [4.6%] subjects)

discontinuations.value: 23.7% for placebo- and 36.0% for lecanemab-treated subjects
discontinuations.quote: Discontinuations occurred in 23.7% for placebo- and 36.0% for lecanemab-treated subjects.

limitations: a small number of symptomatic ARIA-E cases at 10 mg/kg biweekly prompted one Regulatory Authority to request that subsequent ApoE4+ subjects (approximately 70% of the overall study population) not be randomized to the 10 mg/kg biweekly dose.

An additional component to the request required that all ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly who were on study but who had not yet reached 6 months of treatment be immediately discontinued ( N = 25 subjects).

Implementation of these actions led to early (initiated between 300 and 350 randomized participants) and significant changes to the study design that resulted in a marked imbalance in the number of ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly (30% ApoE4+ subjects).

multiplicity.approach: none stated for Bayesian, no correction applied for frequentist
multiplicity.quote: Bayesian analyses did not require adjustment for multiplicity by nature of the Bayesian approach. Conventional analyses were performed using a mixed effects model with repeated measures (MMRM) comparing placebo to active arms. All listed p -values for key secondary endpoints using conventional statistics are nominal, and no correction was applied for multiplicity.

risk_of_bias.judgement: marked imbalance in the number of ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly
risk_of_bias.quote: Implementation of these actions led to early (initiated between 300 and 350 randomized participants) and significant changes to the study design that resulted in a marked imbalance in the number of ApoE4+ subjects on 10 mg/kg biweekly (30% ApoE4+ subjects).
